name_evidence.wording: Wikivoyage has its own town page 'Albany (Western Australia)'; Tourism WA's Great Southern region page names Albany as the region's city.

destinations.name: Torndirrup National Park
destinations.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Torndirrup National Park (park reference point on Frenchman Bay Road; confirm a visitor hub such as The Gap car park)

name_evidence.wording: DBCA park page 'Torndirrup National Park'; Australia's South West listing 'Torndirrup National Park'.
Wikivoyage town page 'Denmark (Western Australia)'; Tourism WA's Great Southern page names Denmark.

destinations.name: Walpole Wilderness
destinations.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Walpole, Western Australia (the base town and visitor centre)

name_evidence.wording: The Walpole Visitor Centre's Explore page calls the area 'the Walpole Wilderness' ('Rising above the Walpole Wilderness, Mount Frankland...', 'At the heart of the Walpole Wilderness, this tranquil marine park...') and lists Conspicuous Cliff, Peaceful Bay, Circular Pool, Fernhook Falls, Mount Frankland and Mandalay Beach under it; Wikipedia has 'Walpole Wilderness Area'. DBCA names Walpole as Walpole-Nornalup NP's base.

destinations.name: Stirling Range National Park
destinations.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Stirling Range National Park (park reference point, near Stirling Range Drive; confirm a visitor hub)

name_evidence.wording: DBCA park page, Tourism WA's Great Southern page and the Australia's South West listing all name 'Stirling Range National Park'.

destinations.name: Fitzgerald River National Park
destinations.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Fitzgerald River National Park (park centroid; the park has no single hub: confirm or recentre on the middle of its spots)

name_evidence.wording: Wikivoyage has a park page 'Fitzgerald River National Park'; DBCA park page of the same name.

spots.name: Princess Royal Fortress
spots.bio: Hilltop fort over King George Sound, where the WWI convoys assembled, and home of the National Anzac Centre museum.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=museum 'Princess Royal Fortress' agreeing with photon
spots.note: Albany's headline: paid fort and museum site of several hours (Wikivoyage, the board's National ANZAC Centre listing). The National Anzac Centre on the same site is this spot, not a second one; the skeptic asks whether to show it as 'National Anzac Centre' for search, left for the owner (Wikipedia's article is 'Princess Royal Fortress').

spots.name: Albany Historic Whaling Station
spots.bio: Whaling station closed in 1978, now a museum with self-guided tours of its flensing decks and the Cheynes IV.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=museum 'Albany‘s Historical Whaling Museum' agreeing with commons
spots.note: Half-day museum at Frenchman Bay listed by Wikivoyage Albany and the board; a city attraction reached on the road to Torndirrup, so it stays with Albany (about 10.5 km from the centre).

spots.name: Mount Clarence
spots.bio: Hill above Albany with walking trails, harbour views and the Desert Mounted Corps Memorial, shipped from Port Said in 1959.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon natural=peak 'Mount Clarence' agreeing with wiki
spots.note: Town hill with trails and the memorial (Wikivoyage, board itinerary); holds the Desert Mounted Corps War Memorial candidate as one spot, as the judge ruled.

spots.name: Two Peoples Bay Nature Reserve
spots.bio: Reserve east of Albany with a visitor centre, trails and lookouts, where the rare Gilbert's potoroo was rediscovered.
spots.note: A nature reserve with only two kept spots (itself and Little Beach), too few for a destination, so it goes under Albany, the base visitors reach it from (about 27 km). Pin at the visitor centre, not Little Beach.

spots.name: Little Beach
spots.bio: Sheltered white-sand beach at Two Peoples Bay, east of Albany, for swimming, diving and canoeing.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon natural=beach 'Little Beach' agreeing with commons
spots.note: Board and DBCA listing; reached from Albany (about 29 km, the farthest Albany spot, inside the 30 km reach).

spots.name: Middleton Beach
spots.bio: Albany's closest town beach, with year-round swimming, a shark net, summer patrols and the Ellen Cove Boardwalk.
spots.note: Visit Albany's lead beach; Ellen Cove (rejected as a duplicate) is part of this spot. Its Noongar name, Binalup, can go in the bio at research.

spots.name: Museum of the Great Southern
spots.bio: Albany's branch of the state museum, with natural and social history galleries and a full-size replica of the brig Amity.
spots.note: Board listing and the WA Museum's page; holds the Residency Museum (rejected as the same site) and is where the Brig Amity replica stands (Brig Amity is in review: if approved it could stay folded in here). Candidate coordinates were the Perth museum: never carried over.

spots.name: Albany Convict Gaol
spots.bio: Restored 1852 convict gaol on Stirling Terrace, its cell blocks now the town's main museum.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=attraction 'Old Albany Gaol, 1852' agreeing with wiki
spots.note: Wikivoyage See listing and Visit Albany heritage page; paid museum in the town centre.

spots.name: West Cape Howe National Park
spots.bio: Coastal park of granite and dolerite cliffs at the southernmost point of mainland Western Australia.
spots.note: A small park with two kept spots (itself and Shelley Beach), too few for a destination; reached from Albany (Visit Albany's national parks page), about 27 km west, inside the 30 km reach. Pin at a visitor point other than Shelley Beach (most of the park is 4WD).

spots.name: Shelley Beach
spots.bio: Crescent beach and campground in West Cape Howe National Park, with a clifftop lookout and a hang-gliding launch.
spots.note: DBCA calls it the most visited area of West Cape Howe; includes Shelley Beach Lookout (rejected as the same stop). About 23-26 km from Albany.

spots.name: Emu Point
spots.bio: Calm, shallow swimming beach on Oyster Harbour with picnic lawns, fishing, boating and windsurfing.
spots.note: Tourism WA attraction page; the visitor point of Oyster Harbour (in review as a near-duplicate of this spot).

spots.name: Albany Wind Farm
spots.bio: Row of 12 wind turbines on the Sandpatch cliffs, with boardwalks, ocean views and a staircase down the cliff.
spots.note: Wikivoyage See listing (open daily, free) and Visit Albany's Quick Top 5.

spots.name: Patrick Taylor Cottage
spots.bio: Wattle-and-daub cottage built about 1832, the oldest surviving dwelling in Western Australia, now a house museum.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon building=yes 'Patrick Taylor Cottage' agreeing with commons, photon, wiki
spots.note: Wikivoyage and Visit Albany heritage page; small museum in the town centre.

spots.name: Gull Rock National Park
spots.bio: Coastal park east of Albany with high lookouts over King George Sound's islands and swimming at Ledge Beach.
spots.note: A one-site park (Ledge Beach, rejected as the same place, is its visitor point), so it is a spot, not a destination; about 11 km from Albany.

spots.name: Nanarup Beach
spots.bio: Surf beach east of Albany with a sheltered swimming lagoon and waterbirds on Taylor Inlet.
spots.note: Visit Albany beaches page; about 18 km from Albany.

spots.name: Frenchman Bay
spots.bio: Sheltered bay on the way to Torndirrup National Park, with calm swimming, snorkelling, barbecues and a picnic area.
spots.note: Visit Albany beaches page. A settlement and beach at the park's edge, not park land: placed with the city (about 10 km), like the whaling station beside it; the owner may move it to Torndirrup.

spots.name: Dog Rock
spots.bio: Granite boulder shaped like a dog's head, with a painted collar, beside Middleton Road in central Albany.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=attraction 'Dog Rock' agreeing with commons, photon, wiki
spots.note: Quirky roadside icon named by Wikivoyage.

spots.name: HMAS Perth Wreck
spots.bio: Former navy ship HMAS Perth, scuttled in King George Sound in 2001 as a dive wreck for certified divers.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon historic=wreck 'Fmr HMAS Perth' agreeing with commons
spots.note: Visit Albany's dive-wreck page; reached with Albany dive operators. Candidate's wiki 'HMAS Perth (1939)' is a different (WWII) ship and does not exist as a title; 'HMAS Perth (D 38)' is the destroyer scuttled off Albany: confirm at research.

spots.name: The Gap and Natural Bridge
spots.bio: Granite chasm where Southern Ocean swells surge below a clifftop viewing platform, beside a natural granite arch.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=viewpoint 'The Gap Lookout' agreeing with commons, photon
spots.note: The park's headline (DBCA, board 'The Gap and Natural Bridge'); one spot with Natural Bridge (rejected as the same attraction). The DBCA site URL in the candidate is a 404, so the link is the park page.

spots.name: Misery Beach
spots.bio: Sheltered beach on the Torndirrup coast, named Australia's best beach in 2022, with a viewing deck and beach stairs.
spots.note: DBCA site page and Visit Albany.

spots.name: Blowholes
spots.bio: Granite blowholes on the Torndirrup coast that spray with a big swell, reached by a 1.6 km return walk.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon tourism=viewpoint 'Blowholes' agreeing with commons
spots.note: DBCA site page and Wikivoyage Albany.

spots.name: Salmon Holes
spots.bio: Lookout over a rocky cove and beach on the Torndirrup Peninsula, where strong rips make the water unsafe for swimming.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon amenity=parking 'Salmon Holes' agreeing with commons, photon
spots.note: DBCA site page and Visit Albany national parks page.

spots.name: Stony Hill
spots.bio: The park's highest point, with a 500 m all-access loop walk and 360-degree views over the coast.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon natural=peak 'Stony Hill' agreeing with commons, photon
spots.note: Named 'Stony Hill' as the judge ruled (DBCA 'Stony Hill and Peak Head', Visit Albany Quick Top 5).

spots.name: Bald Head Walk Trail
spots.bio: Full-day 12.5 km return hike along the Flinders Peninsula to Bald Head and Isthmus Hill.
spots.note: DBCA trail page and Visit Albany's 10 Great Walks. The enumerator's point is a segment near the Salmon Holes start, not the route's midpoint: re-resolve.

spots.name: Jimmy Newells
spots.bio: Short 100 m walk to a viewing platform over a calm, sheltered inlet on the Torndirrup coast.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon amenity=parking 'Jimmy Newells Inlet' agreeing with photon
spots.note: DBCA site page and Visit Albany national parks page.

spots.name: Greens Pool
spots.bio: Sheltered pool of clear water ringed by granite boulders in William Bay National Park, west of Denmark.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon highway=path 'Greens Pool to Elephant Rocks Trail' agreeing with commons, wiki
spots.note: DBCA site, park and board listings; the area's main summer draw.

spots.name: Elephant Rocks
spots.bio: Cove of granite boulders that look like wading elephants, a 10-minute walk from Greens Pool.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon highway=path 'Greens Pool to Elephant Rocks Trail' agreeing with commons, photon
spots.note: DBCA and the board list it separately from Greens Pool. Pin matched a path and Commons: confirm on the cove.

spots.name: William Bay National Park
spots.bio: Coastal park of granite headlands and sheltered bays 14 km west of Denmark, with Madfish Bay and Waterfall Beach.
spots.note: A park with only three spots of its own, so a spot of Denmark (the town visitors base in). Pin at Madfish Bay or Waterfall Beach, not Greens Pool or Elephant Rocks.

spots.name: Ocean Beach
spots.bio: Denmark's patrolled surf beach at the mouth of Wilson Inlet, with a lookout, surf club and walks.
spots.note: Tourism WA attraction page; about 7 km from Denmark.

spots.name: Lights Beach
spots.bio: Surf, fishing and walking beach on the Bibbulmun Track, just east of William Bay National Park.
spots.note: DBCA site page; about 12 km from Denmark.

spots.name: Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk
spots.bio: A 600 m walkway 40 m up in the canopy of the ancient tingle forest, with the Ancient Empire boardwalk below.
spots.note: The headline (DBCA, board); holds the 'Valley of the Giants' board listing (merged, same site). About 15 km east of Walpole.

spots.name: Giant Tingle Tree
spots.bio: Red tingle tree with the largest girth of any living eucalypt, reached by an 800 m circular walk.
spots.note: DBCA site page and the Walpole Visitor Centre; on Hilltop Road (Hilltop Lookout is in review).

spots.name: Conspicuous Cliff
spots.bio: Limestone cliffs and surf beach east of Walpole, with whale-watching lookouts and a Bibbulmun Track day walk.
spots.note: Named Conspicuous Cliff as DBCA and the visitor centre name it (judge's ruling).

spots.name: Circular Pool
spots.bio: Pool and rapids on the Frankland River, with two viewing platforms, a boardwalk and a picnic area.
spots.note: DBCA site page and the Walpole Visitor Centre.

spots.name: Coalmine Beach
spots.bio: Family swimming and paddling beach on Nornalup Inlet, with a picnic area and a boat and kayak launch.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon amenity=parking 'Coalmine Beach Car Park' agreeing with photon
spots.note: DBCA site page and the Walpole Visitor Centre.

spots.name: Peaceful Bay
spots.bio: Coastal village 33 km east of Walpole with turquoise water for swimming, snorkelling and fishing.
spots.note: Walpole Visitor Centre; a beach village with its own draw (not a wrapper). About 19 km in a straight line.

spots.name: Mount Clare
spots.bio: Summit trail through tingle and karri forest to Southern Ocean views, with a picnic area and a Deep River loop.
spots.note: DBCA site page and the visitor centre's half-day walks; the Walpole Mount Clare, not Albany's Mount Clarence (OSM peak about 8 km west of Walpole).

spots.name: Bluff Knoll
spots.bio: Highest peak in southern Western Australia at 1,099 m, with a summit walk and an eastern lookout.
spots.note: The park's headline (DBCA, Tourism WA, board).

spots.name: Toolbrunup Peak
spots.bio: The Stirling Range's second-highest peak, a hard scramble to the summit with 360-degree views.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon natural=peak 'Toolbrunup Peak' agreeing with commons
spots.note: DBCA site and park pages.

spots.name: Mount Trio
spots.bio: Steep summit walk to three peaks linked by a plateau, with a picnic area at the trailhead.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon natural=peak 'Mount Trio' agreeing with photon
spots.note: DBCA site and park pages.

spots.name: Mount Hassell
spots.bio: Moderately difficult summit walk in the Stirling Range, with wildflowers and views to Toolbrunup Peak.
spots.note: DBCA site page; location confirmed inside the park by the judge.

spots.name: Point Ann
spots.bio: Headland with whale-watching platforms where southern right whales calve from June to October, and a heritage trail.
spots.note: DBCA and Wikivoyage; reached from Bremer Bay.

spots.name: West Mount Barren
spots.bio: Peak of the Barren Range with a walk of about 2 hours return and wide views over the park and the coast.
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: photon natural=peak 'West Mount Barren' agreeing with commons
spots.note: DBCA and Wikivoyage.

spots.name: East Mount Barren
spots.bio: A 450 m quartzite peak on the Southern Ocean near Hopetoun, with a hard summit walk and views over the park.
spots.note: DBCA site page; inside Fitzgerald River NP (whole park is this region per the boundary brief), reached from Hopetoun.

spots.name: Quoin Head
spots.bio: Headland on the park's remote coast with a bay, beach and campground, reached by four-wheel drive.
spots.note: DBCA site page; Wikivoyage lists its campsite.

spots.name: Hamersley Inlet
spots.bio: Deep inlet in a winding valley at the end of Hamersley Drive, with birdlife, a beach and a campground.
spots.note: DBCA site page; Wikivoyage lists its campsite.

spots.name: Whalebone Beach
spots.bio: Remote beach between rocky headlands for fishing and walking, reached by four-wheel drive or on foot.
spots.note: DBCA site page.

spots.name: Porongurup National Park
spots.bio: Granite range north of Albany with walking tracks, scenic drives and the Tree in the Rock picnic area.
spots.note: Only two spots of its own (Castle Rock Granite Skywalk, Devils Slide), so not a destination; a national park is never a spot of another park (Stirling Range) and it lies outside Albany's span. Pin at the Tree in the Rock day-use area, not Castle Rock.

spots.name: Castle Rock Granite Skywalk
spots.bio: A 4.4 km return walk up Castle Rock to a suspended skywalk with views to the Stirling Range and the coast.
spots.note: One spot for Castle Rock and the Granite Skywalk (judges: two names for one walk and rock; 'Granite Skywalk' merged). Standalone with the Porongurups.

spots.name: Devils Slide
spots.bio: Walk of 5 km to the Porongurup Range's highest peak, about 2 hours return, with views north and south.
spots.note: DBCA's Porongurup page and Mountain Country Tourism; standalone with the Porongurups.

spots.name: Mount Barker
spots.bio: Service town and gateway to the Porongurup and Stirling ranges, with a visitor centre in the old railway building.
spots.note: Kept as a gateway base (board destination page) but its draws are the Porongurups and Stirlings; with three Porongurup spots it is under the four-spot bar, so it stands alone. Low priority (the skeptic's 'gateway at a low rank').

spots.name: Bremer Bay
spots.bio: Coastal town at the mouth of Bremer Bay, base for the Bremer Canyon orca season and Fitzgerald River National Park.
spots.note: Board destination page; a gateway town 54 km from Fitzgerald River NP's centre, outside its span (and a town is not a spot of a park it lies outside). The orca trips are operators, mentioned in the bio only.

spots.name: Katanning
spots.bio: Wheatbelt-edge town with an oversized all-ages playground, a saleyards viewing platform and the Premier Mill Hotel.
spots.note: Kept as a town with draws of its own (the playground is in review as a separate spot, so it is named in the town's bio). No destination within 100 km.

spots.name: The Kodja Place
spots.bio: Cultural centre in Kojonup with the Kodj Gallery, the Storyplace, the Australian Rose Maze and Noongar stories.
spots.note: Board listing; in Kojonup on Albany Highway, far from any destination. Candidate note wrongly placed it in Albany.

spots.name: Yongergnow Australian Malleefowl Centre
spots.bio: Volunteer-run centre in Ongerup on the mallee and its malleefowl, with a captive-raising program, gallery and café.
spots.note: Lonely Planet and the board; spelt 'Yongergnow' as the brief requires. In Ongerup, about 55-60 km north-east of the Stirling Range, outside every span.

spots.name: Cheynes Beach
spots.bio: Beach east of Albany with clifftop views, winter whale watching, a salmon run and wildflowers.
spots.note: Board listing and Visit Albany; about 50 km east of Albany (50 minutes), outside its 30 km reach, and not part of any park destination.

spots.name: Mandalay Beach
spots.bio: Remote beach in D'Entrecasteaux National Park with whale-watching platforms and the 1911 Mandalay wreck at low tide.
spots.coordinates_source: OSM tourism=viewpoint "Mandalay Beach" (via Photon; confirm with resolve-pin.py)
spots.note: Moved here at reconciliation. Reached from Walpole (wa-great-southern), 77 km from the Southern Forests centre; no wa-south-west destination is near. If wa-great-southern proposes a Walpole or Walpole-Nornalup destination whose span reaches it, it becomes that destination's spot.

spots.name: Fernhook Falls
spots.bio: Deep River cascades over granite into Rowell's Pool in the Walpole forests, with walk trails and boardwalks.
spots.coordinates_source: OSM waterway=waterfall "Fernhook Falls" (via Photon; confirm with resolve-pin.py)
spots.note: Moved here at reconciliation. 66 km from the Southern Forests centre and reached from Walpole (wa-great-southern); standalone unless a Walpole destination there takes it.

spots.name: Mount Frankland National Park
spots.bio: Granite peak in the Walpole Wilderness with a summit walk to a lookout over karri and tingle forest.
spots.coordinates_source: needs the Mount Frankland Wilderness Lookout car park (Towerman's Hut) from OSM or DBCA, not the park centroid
spots.note: Moved here at reconciliation. A small park (the judge: a standalone spot, not a destination); reached from Walpole (wa-great-southern), about 75 km from Pemberton. Standalone unless a Walpole destination there takes it.
